title: NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own) — Assignment of a Policy to the Buyer of the Building
content:
### Assignment on sale — NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)

When the insured building is sold, the seller may assign the in-force policy to the buyer instead of cancelling it.

- **Authority.** An assignment is processed only on the seller's signed assignment request on file naming the buyer, and only on a policy whose status is in force. Both are read from Tidemark's records: the signed request on the request records, and the status on the policy record.
- **The buyer.** The buyer must already have a customer profile with Tidemark, becomes the named insured from the title transfer date, and keeps the policy number, term, limits and deductibles; there is no waiting period and no new premium at assignment.
- **What is recorded.** The buyer's mortgagee, loan number, mortgage requirement, premium payor and primary-residence designation are recorded at assignment.
- **Tiers.** A tenant contents policy cannot be assigned. Assignment is open on the NFIP Dwelling Form – Residential Condominium Unit, – Manufactured Home, – Secondary Single-Family Home, – Primary Single-Family Home and – Two-to-Four Unit Building tiers.
- **HFIAA surcharge.** When the buyer's primary-residence designation differs from the seller's, the HFIAA surcharge for the current term stays as booked and the buyer's designation applies from the next renewal.

| Request and record | Assignment |
|---|---|
| Seller's signed request naming the buyer on file, policy in force, buyer has a Tidemark profile, tier other than Tenant Contents | Processed; no waiting period, no new premium |
| No signed request naming the buyer on file | Not processed |
| Policy status other than in force | Not processed |
| Tenant Contents policy | Cannot be assigned |

*Hypothetical case.* A seller whose policy was designated a primary residence assigns it to a buyer who will not live in the home. The current term's HFIAA surcharge stays as booked; the buyer's non-primary designation applies from the next renewal.
